meta.description: Held-out error of the Blender residual models, one median residual per product, against the cores-times-clock (CPU) or shaders-times-clock (GPU) baseline, overall and by vendor, family, generation and (GPU) backend.

sources.name: Blender Open Data benchmark snapshots
sources.licence: CC0 (Creative Commons Zero), stated on https://opendata.blender.org/download/ and in the LICENSE.txt shipped in each snapshot. No conditions on reuse; the site credits it anyway.
sources.frequency: weekly collection; snapshots are regenerated daily

limitations: Blender Open Data is crowd-submitted: cooling, memory and drivers are not controlled.
Scores come from a single Blender version and are never combined across versions.
The Blender residual model is separate from the SPEC models: it predicts a Blender rendering score from specifications, and its verdicts say nothing about SPEC workloads.
Rendering rewards cores, clocks and power limits; cache-heavy parts such as AMD's X3D chips can look like underperformers here and still lead in games.

CPU and GPU specifications come from tables maintained in this repository (pdi/tech_value/cpu_specs.py, pdi/tech_value/gwpg.py), entered from manufacturers' reference specifications. Factory-overclocked cards are measured but share one spec row.
Predicted scores and residuals are this site's estimates. Blender Open Data is CC0; the Blender Foundation is credited and does not endorse these estimates.
